title.narrative: Result 4: A bipartisan, women caucusoriented advocacy campaign mainstreams gender sensitive economic development towards policy makers

description.narrative: Extending the circle of engagement under Result 4, the partners will, together with provincial women leaders and LAs champions, extend the influence sphere to the national level. To do so, MONES will initially study the National Gender strategies, plans and implementation (A4.1) and enrich the document with findings and learning from the local level (A1.1, A2.1, A3.2) to gather hard data to be disseminated to policy makers (A4.2). On this basis, an advocacy campaign will be rolled out in Ulaanbaatar by creating & mentoring a Local, Provincial and National Champions platform (A4.3) and supporting those champions to voiceout to National Authorities, parties, MPs about best practices, gaps, evidencebased recommendations through high level events and fora.Harnessed to strong business cases, hard evidences and good field practices, it is expected that the influence of women knowledge networks will increase together with awareness of policy shapers at national level.

title.narrative: Result 3: Womens groups are empowered in their dialogue capacities with Local Authorities for mutual support and conducive local policies

description.narrative: The partners, under Result 3, will focus on building the case for more supportive Local Authorities & more responsive province & soumlevels policies. Led by MONES, AVSF and GERES will create, animate and mentor a network of women leaders from CSOs but also activist groups in raising their voice, concerns and interests at local level (A3.1; A3.2) leading to an improved nurtured partnership between this network and Women LAs & Representatives (A3.3). Additionally, the Action will provide an RBA gender equity training (A3.4) to all CSO members and LAs, irrespective of sex to bring stakeholders on par and specifically create a Farmers & Herders Women Council (A3.5) designed to induce policies and plans responsive to the promoted production systems.Anchored on R1 and R2 outputs, it is foreseen that the awareness and influence of key women leaders networks will increase and reflect on policy shapers at local and provincial levels.

title.narrative: Result 1: Womens groups are empowered in their role in income generating activities, rural cooperatives and household financial management

description.narrative: Under Result 1, the consortium led by MONES experts will produce evidence (Study A1.1) to further design an informed and contextualise mobilisation strategy towards the CSOs. The partners will then rollout an initial blanket capacity building activity (A1.2), followed by more specific women leadership training (A1.3), and specific support on financial literacy and participation (A1.4) addressing key gaps. To further strengthen womens role and participation in the Action, exposures visits will be organised amongst peers to showcase successes and opportunities (A1.5).With the Gender study considered as key input, it is expected that mobilisation, capacities and skills of target CSOs and women will be increased.

title.narrative: Result 2: High potential agriculture value chains (organic vegetable and sustainable cashmere) are supported for economic empowerment of womens groups

description.narrative: Under Result 2, the consortium led by GERES/AVSF, will produce evidence and a practical methodology on innovative organic vegetable and sustainable cashmere production (A2.1) further informed by the gender study (A1.1). This body of knowledge will be disseminated to CSOs in the form of training materials (A2.2). Following a mobilisation strategy adapted to economic development, the partners will roll out a Training of Trainers (A2.3) to ground the knowledge in each target CSO, specific technical support and seed funding for selected motivated farmers groups in vegetable production (A2.4) and herders Coops in sustainable cashmere production (A2.5). Eventually, to ensure rapid uptake of the innovative production systems, subgrants and individualised technical assistance will be allocated to a limited number of producers groups (A2.6).Grounding the work package with the value chain capitalisation as key input, it is expected that mobilisation, capacities and skills of target CSOs and their women members will be enhanced.
